definition: Email Service Provider — a platform used to send, manage, and measure newsletter or marketing campaigns (e.g. Beehiiv, Substack, ConvertKit).
The percentage of delivered emails that were opened. Increasingly noisy due to Apple Mail Privacy Protection.
Click-Through Rate — the percentage of recipients who clicked one or more links in a newsletter issue.
Growing an email audience through opt-in forms, lead magnets, referrals, cross-promotion, and content upgrades.
A subscription flow that requires the subscriber to confirm via a follow-up email before they are added to the list.
The ability for legitimate newsletter email to reach the inbox rather than spam or promotions folders.
Sender Policy Framework — a DNS record that lists which servers are allowed to send email for a domain.
DomainKeys Identified Mail — a cryptographic signature that proves an email was authorized by the sending domain.
Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance — a policy for SPF/DKIM failures and reporting.
Gradually increasing send volume from a new domain or IP so mailbox providers learn to trust the sender.
Paid placement in a newsletter issue — a common monetization model for independent publishers.
Charging readers a recurring fee for premium newsletter content or an ad-free experience.
A free resource (checklist, PDF, mini-course) offered in exchange for an email address.
Incentives for existing subscribers to invite others, often unlocking bonus content or swag.
An automated series of emails sent after someone subscribes, introducing the brand and setting expectations.
